children: TIME TO STRADDLE MIDTERM VOLATILITY

With the summer all but over, strategists are turning their attention to the big event of the year — the November 3 midterm elections. With 35 Senate seats and all 435 House of Representatives seats up for grabs, strategists at Evercore ISI, including Julian Emanuel, are preparing for some volatility and uncertainty.

Emanuel, managing director leading the firm's equity, derivatives & quantitative strategy team, was the lead author of a note pointing out on Monday that the midterms "are generally unkind to the party in the White House." While the average is a loss of about 28 House seats, he notes that President Donald Trump's Republican party lost 41 in 2018 while Biden's Democrats lost nine seats in 2022.

And with the Republicans currently holding a narrow 219-seat House majority and a 53-47 majority in the Senate, Emanuel writes that everything is "in play" with the Democrats widely expected to reclaim the House while expectations are less clear for the Senate.
But whatever happens he notes that when the party controlling one or both branches of Congress is not the same as the party of the sitting President, this causes uncertainty for the market.

While a House flip would add uncertainty, "a Senate flip would magnify the dynamic as Democrats would have veto power over nominations while President Trump’s predisposition toward exercising Executive Authority would likely only increase."
Emanuel quoted Benjamin Franklin saying, "In this world nothing can be certain except
death and taxes.” But to those two, the strategist added a rising National Debt and more equity market volatility.
So far, however, relatively low levels of market volatility have boosted the attractiveness of options as a way for investors to position for an uptick in price swings headed into the midterms.

So Emanuel recommended buying options straddles on the SPY, the ETF that tracks the S&P 500 — a strategy designed to profit from a rise in volatility by combining the purchase of a put and a call option.
He recommended purchasing SPY November contracts at the 770 strike price, with the position standing to profit if the S&P 500 gains or falls by about 5% or more by the November expiration.

In a nod to interest rate risk, the strategists also recommended buying defensive November put contracts at the 82 strike on the long-term U.S. Treasury bond ETF, positioning for a rise in volatility through November.
(Sinéad Carew, Saqib Iqbal Ahmed)
